author: Hough, Frank O.; Ludwig, Verle E.; Shaw, Henry I., Jr.
title: History of U.S. Marine Corps Operations in World War II, Volume I: Pearl Harbor to Guadalcanal
publisher: Historical Branch, G-3 Division, Headquarters, U.S. Marine Corps, Washington, D.C.
notes: The first of the Marine Corps' five volumes: the interwar development of amphibious doctrine and landing craft — the part of the story that explains why any of the later landings were possible — then Wake, the Philippines and Guadalcanal to February 1943. Cite it beside source:miller-1949 rather than instead of it; each service wrote the campaign it fought. The title page carries no year, only Library of Congress card number 58-60002; 1958 is taken from that and from the Internet Archive's record of the volume. Same reachability note as source:morton-1962 — the official Marine Corps host is not openly reachable from here and the url is the HyperWar transcription, whose text carries the printed page numbers.
